title: Paul Graham on judging founders, boosting ambition, and YC interviews (Conversations with Tyler)
summary: Graham explains how he evaluates early-stage founders (people over plans, determination via stories, real understanding), why YC interviews work in about 10 minutes, and how he pushes founders to think bigger. He also covers obsessing over missed companies and how fame arrived at YC unnoticed.

principles.text: The earlier the stage, the more you are judging the founders rather than the business plan.
principles.quote: the earlier you're judging startups the more you're just judging the founders

principles.text: Judge determination from stories of what people did when things went wrong, not from how tough they act.
principles.quote: the way you tell determination is not so much from talking to them as from asking them stories about things that have happened to them that's where you can see determination

principles.text: Test whether founders truly understand their idea versus having a newspaper-level grasp of it.
principles.quote: I can tell if people know what they're talking about when they come and talk about some idea especially some technical idea

principles.text: Help founders think bigger by asking how an idea could be larger; pushing costs the advisor no effort.
principles.quote: there is a skill to it to take an idea and say okay so here's an idea so how could this be bigger

principles.text: Working with someone for a few minutes reveals most of what you need; minds rarely flip after about seven minutes.
principles.quote: you see what it's like to work with people by working with them for 10 minutes and that's enough it turns out

principles.text: Obsess over failure cases and fix process flaws immediately, e.g. require two reviewers per application.
principles.quote: after that every application had to be seen by at least two people
